common_name: Duchess Pink Torenia (Compact Pink Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set out transplants once frost danger has passed, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Duchess is Syngenta's wide-range wishbone flower line bred for early, uniform flowering across its full color set.

directions: Set plants into consistently moist, well-drained, fertile soil in partial to full shade, spacing them 8-10 inches apart for a tidy mounded mass. Duchess Pink carries clear soft-pink tubular flowers with the characteristic fused, wishbone-shaped stamens tucked inside each bloom, distinguishing it from the bicolor Duchess Blue and White and deep violet Duchess Royal Indigo already grown in this dataset. The compact, well-branched habit holds its shape without pinching and flowers continuously from late spring through frost with no deadheading. Keep soil evenly damp through summer heat, since torenia's shallow root system dries out and stalls flowering faster than most bedding annuals.
sources: Syngenta Flowers - Duchess Torenia Series Product Information
University of Florida IFAS Extension - Torenia fournieri for Florida Shade Gardens

common_name: Duchess Deep Blue Torenia (Compact Violet-Blue Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set out transplants once frost danger has passed, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this Duchess selection carries the deepest, most saturated blue-violet tone in the series.

directions: Plant into consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, spacing 8-10 inches apart for a dense mounded planting. Duchess Deep Blue produces a solid, richly saturated violet-blue flower rather than a bicolor pattern, giving it a bolder, more uniform block of color than the two-tone Duchess Blue and White already cataloged here. Growth stays low and well-branched all season, blooming from late spring to frost without deadheading. Because torenia's roots sit shallowly in the soil, mulch around plantings to buffer soil moisture swings during hot, dry stretches.
sources: Syngenta Flowers - Duchess Torenia Series Product Information

common_name: Duchess Burgundy Torenia (Compact Wine-Red Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set out transplants once frost danger has passed, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Duchess Burgundy is part of Syngenta's eight-color Duchess breeding line, one of the broadest color ranges bred into torenia.

directions: Grow in consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, setting plants 8-10 inches apart so the compact mounds knit together into a solid carpet of color. Duchess Burgundy bears deep wine-red flowers with the fused wishbone-shaped stamens typical of the genus, giving it a richer, darker tone than the pink or blue Duchess selections already in this dataset. It flowers heavily and continuously from spring through fall frost without any deadheading needed. Provide steady moisture and a light monthly feeding, since inconsistent watering causes torenia's flower count to drop off quickly in hot weather.
sources: Syngenta Flowers - Duchess Torenia Series Product Information
University of Florida IFAS Extension - Torenia fournieri for Florida Shade Gardens

common_name: Kauai Blue and White Torenia (Compact Bicolor Shade Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kauai Blue and White is part of a compact, early-flowering PanAmerican Seed wishbone flower series bred for uniform bloom timing across its color range.

directions: Set transplants into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, spacing plants 8-10 inches apart for a dense mounded display. Kauai Blue and White pairs a violet-blue upper lip with a white lower lip and throat, giving it a crisper, more contrasting bicolor pattern than the solid-colored Kauai Burgundy and Kauai Deep Blue already grown in this dataset. Like its series-mates it stays compact and well-branched, blooming continuously from late spring through frost with strong heat and humidity tolerance and no deadheading required. Keep the root zone evenly moist, since dry spells quickly slow bud production on this shallow-rooted annual.
sources: PanAmerican Seed - Kauai Torenia Series Grower Information

common_name: Clown Burgundy Torenia (Deep Wine Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost or set out transplants once frost danger has passed; Clown Burgundy belongs to an older, well-established wishbone flower series distinct from the newer Duchess and Kauai lines already represented here.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, setting plants closer together at 6-9 inches than most torenia series to fill in as a solid mass planting. Clown Burgundy produces deep wine-red flowers on a slightly bushier, more traditional torenia habit than the extra-compact modern Duchess and Kauai selections already cataloged here. It blooms heavily from late spring through fall frost without deadheading, and while bred primarily for shade, established plantings tolerate a few hours of morning sun in humid climates without scorching. Water regularly to keep the soil from drying out between rains, since torenia's shallow roots have little buffer against drought stress.
sources: PanAmerican Seed - Clown Torenia Series Grower Information
Dave's Garden - Torenia, the Clown Flower

common_name: Summer Wave Large Violet Torenia (Trailing Large-Flowered Shade Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed into moist, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; this Suntory-bred trailing selection carries a deeper violet tone than the Amethyst and Blue selections already grown in this dataset.

directions: Grow in consistently moist, fertile, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, letting the trailing stems spill from baskets, window boxes, or raised bed edges. Summer Wave Large Violet carries deep violet-purple, large-throated flowers, giving it a cooler, more saturated tone than the reddish-purple of Summer Wave Large Amethyst already in this dataset. The self-cleaning, heat-tolerant habit needs no deadheading and keeps blooming from spring into fall, spreading two to three feet wide despite a modest mounded height. Feed lightly on a monthly basis and avoid letting containers sit waterlogged, since the vigorous trailing growth is prone to root rot in soggy, poorly drained mix.
sources: Proven Winners - Summer Wave Large Violet Torenia Grower Information
University of Florida IFAS Gardening Solutions - Torenia

common_name: Mayan Purple Mexican Petunia (Sterile Compact Ruellia)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring once soil has warmed, in any well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; Mayan Purple is one of three sterile, patented Mexican petunia cultivars bred at the University of Florida specifically to eliminate the seed-borne invasiveness of the wild species.

directions: Plant in any well-drained to moist garden soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing 12-18 inches apart for a mid-size mounded clump. Mayan Purple produces the classic rich violet-purple, funnel-shaped bloom of Mexican petunia on a plant bred to set no viable seed, so it spreads only by its clump gradually widening rather than by the aggressive self-sowing that makes the unimproved species invasive in Gulf Coast natural areas. It stays noticeably shorter and tidier than seed-grown Ruellia simplex, tolerating heat, humidity, and short dry spells with minimal care once roots are established. Shear lightly in midsummer if stems stretch, to keep the clump dense and encourage a fresh round of bloom.
sources: University of Florida IFAS - Mayan Series Ruellia Simplex Release Information
HortScience - Fruitless Ruellia simplex Cultivar Development

common_name: Mayan White Mexican Petunia (Sterile Compact White-Flowered Ruellia)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring once soil has warmed, in any well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; Mayan White is a sterile, patented UF-bred selection released alongside Mayan Purple to expand the non-invasive color range of Mexican petunia.

directions: Grow in any well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade, setting plants 12-18 inches apart to fill into a rounded clump within a season. Mayan White carries clean white, funnel-shaped flowers, a distinctly different color niche from the purple, pink, and lavender Ruellia simplex selections already in this dataset, while sharing the same sterile breeding that keeps it from seeding into surrounding beds or natural areas. The compact habit stays well under two feet, tolerating heat, humidity, and brief drought once established with little maintenance beyond an occasional midsummer shearing. Its white flowers show up especially well against dark foliage companions or in evening gardens.
sources: University of Florida IFAS - Mayan Series Ruellia Simplex Release Information
HortScience - Fruitless Ruellia simplex Cultivar Development

common_name: Mayan Pink Mexican Petunia (Sterile Compact Pink-Flowered Ruellia)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring once soil has warmed, in any well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; Mayan Pink was released a year after Mayan Purple and Mayan White to complete UF's sterile Mexican petunia color trio.

directions: Plant in any well-drained to moist garden soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing 12-18 inches apart for a solid mounded clump by midseason. Mayan Pink bears soft rose-pink, funnel-shaped flowers on the same sterile, non-seeding plant developed for the Mayan breeding line, filling a color gap left by the purple and white selections already in this dataset. It keeps a compact, well-branched form well under two feet tall and shows strong tolerance of heat, humidity, and short dry spells once its roots are established. A light midsummer shearing keeps the clump dense and refreshes bloom for the second half of the season.
sources: University of Florida IFAS - Mayan Series Ruellia Simplex Release Information
HortScience - Fruitless Ruellia simplex Cultivar Development
